correctness.rationale: The outward facet normals have horizontal component cos(theta) along the base-edge outward bisector and vertical component ±sin(theta). Adjacent same-sign faces have dot product 1−2s²cos²(theta); opposite faces on an equatorial edge enclose the normal angle theta_++theta_-. Thus minimizing the largest interior angle is maximizing min(2m,g(m+D/2)), with g(x)=2 asin(s cos x) and D/2<m<pi/2−D/2. The latter term is strictly decreasing and tends to zero at the upper endpoint; the increasing term can cross it in the open interval only if D<g(D). Solving the latter condition gives exactly the positive root of 2s z²+z−s=0 for z=sin(D/2), and solving the crossing gives the stated tangent formula. At equality of the endpoint values the objective already decreases strictly on the open interval, so the second branch, including the transition, is not attained; the smaller elevation tends to zero and its height to infinity. At D=0 the crossing is at arctan(s). At any other m the symmetric objective is already strictly smaller, and at m=arctan(s) a positive D strictly decreases the g term, proving global uniqueness. The equality heights are Rc/s, and both equatorial and spoke angles then agree. Differentiating the crossing gives beta'(0+)=s²/(1+s²).

evidence: The antiprism theorem minimizes the largest of 4n interior ridge angles and attains equidihedrality, but has two twisted bases and no apex pair. The equilibrium-transition theorem has two independently variable positive bipyramid heights but optimizes no dihedral quantity and parameterizes a different scalar.

value.rationale: The comparison is meaningful within a natural polyhedron family: controlling the largest dihedral angle selects one similarity class and makes every edge angle equal, while imposing a geometric asymmetry gives an exact price and a threshold beyond which no finite optimizer exists. These are usable benchmarks for dihedral-angle extremal geometry, not just a numerical angle at a prescribed height.
residual_risks: No comparison to optimal values in arbitrary combinatorial types is implied.
